In [[abstract algebra]], '''Krull's separation lemma''' is a [[Lemma (mathematics)|lemma]] in [[ring theory]]. It was proved by [[Wolfgang Krull]] in 1928.<ref name="Krull1928">{{cite journal|last1=Krull|first1=Wolfgang|title=Zur Theorie der zweiseitigen Ideale in nichtkommutativen Bereichen|journal=Mathematische Zeitschrift|volume=28|issue=1|year=1928|pages=481–503|issn=0025-5874|doi=10.1007/BF01181179|s2cid=122870138 }}</ref>

==Statement of the lemma==
Let <math>I</math> be an [[Ideal (ring theory)|ideal]] and let <math>M</math> be a multiplicative system (''i.e.'' <math>M</math> is closed under multiplication) in a [[Ring (mathematics)|ring]] <math>R</math>, and suppose 
<math>I  \cap M = \varnothing</math>. Then there exists a [[prime ideal]] <math>P</math> satisfying <math>I \subseteq P</math> and <math>P  \cap M = \varnothing</math>.<ref>{{cite journal|author=Sun, Shu-Hao|title=On separation lemmas|journal=Journal of Pure and Applied Algebra|volume=78|issue=3|year=1992|pages=301–310|doi=10.1016/0022-4049(92)90112-S|doi-access=free}}</ref>
